title: Roy Fielding's Dissertation and the Origin of REST (2000)
explainer: 'REST' isn't just a synonym for 'JSON over HTTP' - it's an architectural style Roy Fielding defined precisely in his 2000 UC Irvine doctoral dissertation, 'Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures.' Fielding, who was also one of the authors of the HTTP specification itself, described REST as a set of constraints - statelessness, a uniform interface built around resources, layered systems, and more - meant to explain why the web's architecture scaled so well, not as a prescription for how to shape API URLs. That history is why a genuinely 'RESTful' API is a claim about architectural properties like statelessness and resource-orientation, which is exactly what addressing and persisting multiple resource types in this lesson is practicing.
